source_of_truth: Read by hand in app/components/forms/SearchControls.vue: the same semantic defect -- a form control with no accessible name -- appears in four markup forms. The native <input> (line 8), <select> (line 9) and <textarea> (line 10) each have no <label for>, no wrapping <label>, no aria-label, no aria-labelledby and no title, so each is a confirmed form-control-without-label that the semantic engine proves. The fourth control is a custom <div role="textbox" contenteditable> (line 11) with no name: the identical defect in a non-native syntax. ui-audit deliberately judges only native elements for names, so it does not cover custom ARIA widgets; that control's missing name is listed out_of_scope (a documented blind spot, not an unfair miss). Derived from the markup, not from the tool.

expected.rationale: native <input type="text"> with no accessible name by any mechanism; proven by the semantic element tree.
native <select> with no accessible name; same defect as the input, different tag, so the rule must fire identically.
native <textarea> with no accessible name; same defect, third syntactic form.

coverage_gaps.what: custom <div role="textbox" contenteditable> with no accessible name
coverage_gaps.why_out_of_scope: ui-audit judges accessible names only on native HTML elements (it iterates !e.isComponent and its header scopes to native markup), so it does not cover custom ARIA widgets. This is a real accessibility defect the tool does not claim to catch: surfaced here as a known coverage gap (counted in cov-gap, excluded from recall) so the miss is visible rather than hidden.
